written_from: IBM z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385), read by section (page numbers are not cited): the PROC statement and symbolic parameters (EXEC / PROC / SET value assignment), the SET statement, the EXEC statement's PARM.procstepname and COND.procstepname parameters, DD statement overrides and added DDs in a procedure call, the INCLUDE statement, the JCLLIB statement (ORDER), and the IF/THEN/ELSE/ENDIF relational expression (stepname.procstepname.RC / RUN / ABENDCC). Expected answers were written before any resolver ran on them.
flow_jcl: //* #8413 slice 2: PROC resolution (symbolic parameters and defaults,
//* SET, EXEC PARM. / COND. overrides of a PROC step, a DD override, a
//* DD added to a PROC step, INCLUDE, JCLLIB ORDER) and
//* stepname.procstepname tests inside IF. The resolved step lists
//* and the run / bypass answers are in scenarios.json, written from
//* IBM's z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385) before any evaluator ran
//* on them. Library members: "libraries" in scenarios.json.
resolve_input: resolve: the call step of a job, e.g. S1 of SYMJOB; libraries are the libraries object of this file.
resolve_answer: expect: per proc step (key CALLSTEP.PROCSTEP, or CALLSTEP for a plain step), pgm; parm and cond only where the scenario is about them; dd = every DD naming a DSN, in the order the step ends up with them, as {ddname: dsn}.
flow_input: given: per step that starts, {rc: n} or {abend: code}, keyed by CALLSTEP.PROCSTEP for a procedure's step.
flow_answer: expect: per step in execution order, run or bypass.

resolve.basis: Symbolic parameters, PROC statement: a value coded on the PROC statement is the default and is used when the calling EXEC assigns none. &HLQ..IN.&SUF: the first period ends the symbolic name, the second is the literal period, so PROD.IN.DATA; the PARM operand's quotes do not stop substitution of &PRM.

A value assigned on the calling EXEC overrides the PROC statement default, in every procedure statement that names the symbolic, steps P1 and P2 alike. SUF is not assigned, so its default DATA stands.
EXEC PROC=CATP is the keyword form of EXEC CATP. Only SUF is assigned; HLQ and PRM keep their PROC statement defaults.
SET statement: it assigns a value to a symbolic parameter used in the JCL statements that follow it, up to the next SET of the same name.
SET statement: the second SET of QUAL replaces the first for the statements after it; D1 above keeps PAYR.
A call that overrides nothing resolves to the procedure's statements as written.

EXEC PARM.procstepname= and COND.procstepname= replace the PARM and COND on that procedure step only; the new COND replaces the old one, it does not add a test (so (4,LT,A1) is gone). A1 is not named, so it keeps PARM X1 and has no COND.

DD statement in a calling job, procstepname.ddname form: it overrides the procedure step's DD of that name (the DSN is replaced, A1's other DD SYSUT2 is untouched). A DD whose ddname the procedure step lacks (A2.EXTRA) is added to that step, after the procedure's own DDs; overrides precede added DDs and follow the order of the procedure's steps.
JCLLIB statement: the system searches the libraries in ORDER, in the order coded; PRC1 is in both LIB.A and LIB.B and the first library, LIB.A, supplies it.
JCLLIB statement: a member absent from the first library is looked for in the next; PRC2 is only in LIB.B.
As jcllib-first-library-wins with ORDER=(LIB.B,LIB.A): the same member now comes from LIB.B.
PRC3 is both an in-stream procedure and in LIB.A. ASSUMED A1: the in-stream procedure is used.
LIBJOB2 has no in-stream PRC3, so the search reaches LIB.A (the second library) and finds it.
INCLUDE statement: the statements of the member replace the INCLUDE, so the member's DD belongs to the step above. ASSUMED A2: INCLUDE searches the JCLLIB ORDER libraries first-wins, as EXEC does.

flow.basis: IF relational expression, stepname.procstepname.RC: R1.Q1.RC = 0 and R1.Q2.RC <= 4 are both true, so the THEN clause R2 runs and R3 (ELSE) does not. R1.Q2.RUN = TRUE: Q2 ran. ABENDCC = S0C7: nothing abended, false. R6 COND (4,LT,R1.Q2): 4 < 0 false, runs.
Q2's own COND (4,LT,Q1): 4 < 0 false, Q2 runs. R1.Q2.RC <= 4 is false, so the ELSE clause R3 runs. R6 COND (4,LT,R1.Q2): 4 < 8, bypass.

Q2's COND (4,LT,Q1): 4 < 8 true, Q2 is bypassed. R1.Q1.RC = 0 false, so R3. R1.Q2.RUN = TRUE: Q2 did not run, false, so R4 is bypassed. R6: the COND test names a bypassed step, which is false (IBM: a bypassed step tests false), so R6 runs.

Q2 has no EVEN / ONLY, so it is bypassed after the abend. R1.Q1.ABENDCC = S0C7 is true, R5 runs. R6 has no EVEN / ONLY, bypassed. ASSUMED A3 (as ifelse A3): the two IFs that do not name ABEND or ABENDCC are not evaluated after an abend, so R2, R3 and R4 start nothing.
As ifp-q1-abends-s0c7, but R1.Q1.ABENDCC = S0C7 is false for S806, so R5 is bypassed too.

assumed.text: An in-stream procedure is used in preference to a library member of the same name (the manual's search order for EXEC procname was not verified against the text; stated from the JCL Reference's description of the procedure search).
INCLUDE searches the libraries named on JCLLIB ORDER in order, first library wins, as an EXEC procedure name does.
After an ordinary abend an IF construct that does not name ABEND or ABENDCC starts nothing (same as tests/equivalence/jcl/ifelse A3).

refused.construct: unqualified PARM= or COND= on an EXEC that calls a procedure
refused.why: its effect on the procedure's other steps is a separate rule not answered here; only the procstepname forms are

refused.construct: a SET value for a symbolic that the PROC statement also defaults
refused.why: precedence between SET and the PROC default is not answered here
the null-value rule is not answered here

refused.construct: nested procedure calls, INCLUDE inside a procedure, a DD override that changes a DD's kind (DSN to SYSOUT or DUMMY)
